questions.cardText:
[Art History] What happened to Vincent van Gogh’s ear after he cut it off?
A. He buried it in his garden
B. He kept it in his closet
C. He gave it to someone
Answer: C. After cutting off a portion of his ear, Vincent van Gogh presented it to a woman working as a maid at a local brothel. She fainted on the spot.
questions.en: To whom did Vincent van Gogh give the piece of his ear he had cut off in Arles in December 1888, a young woman working as a maid at a local brothel?
questions.de: Wem schenkte Vincent van Gogh das Stück seines Ohrs, das er sich im Dezember 1888 in Arles abgeschnitten hatte – einer jungen Frau, die als Dienstmädchen in einem örtlichen Bordell arbeitete?

timeline.labelEn: Van Gogh cuts off part of his left ear in Arles and hands it to a woman at a brothel
timeline.labelDe: Van Gogh schneidet sich in Arles einen Teil des linken Ohrs ab und übergibt es einer Frau in einem Bordell

questions.notes: Identified by Bernadette Murphy (2016) as Gabrielle Berlatier, a 17-year-old cleaning girl; older accounts call her 'Rachel', a prostitute — accept either.

questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Inventions] Why was the QWERTY layout designed to be the way they are today?
A. To prevent jamming in typewriters
B. To increase typing speed
C. To standardize keyboards for all languages
Answer: A. The layout was designed to prevent jamming by separating commonly used letter combinations.
questions.en: For which typewriter, the first commercially successful one, was the QWERTY keyboard layout developed?
questions.de: Für welche Schreibmaschine, die erste kommerziell erfolgreiche, wurde die QWERTY-Tastaturbelegung entwickelt?

timeline.labelEn: Remington's mechanics finalise the QWERTY layout for the Sholes and Glidden typewriter
timeline.labelDe: Remingtons Mechaniker legen die QWERTY-Belegung für die Sholes-and-Glidden-Schreibmaschine endgültig fest

questions.notes: The card's jamming explanation is popular but disputed (Wikipedia calls it possibly invented or incorrect; the layout may come from telegraph operators' feedback), so the question asks the verifiable origin instead.
